newsitem.title: USA: US spot resids steady to up again on weather,crude.
newsitem.headline: US spot resids steady to up again on weather,crude.

text.p: U.S. spot fuel oil prices were unchanged to up slightly again Tuesday in moderate trade, with firmer crude and some East Coast utility demand after the recent heat wave still underpinning the complex, sources said.

"Utilities have been out looking for some oil. Gas may be cheaper but it's still not that reliable and you need a backup guarantee which is oil," said one East Coast utility source, noting some eastern gas pipelines recently cut interruptible and some secondary firm supplies.
In New York Harbor, physical one percent firmed a quarter to $16.50-75 a barrel or higher, traders said.
NYH July one percent paper rose another 15-20 cents to about $17 after further gains in NYMEX crude.
NYH 0.3 high pour held relatively steady in the $18.25 area, but traders said the grade seemed well supported amid reports some utilities were looking to increase contract takes.
High sulphurs in New York also scored modest gains, with 2.2 percent now quoted near the $15 mark.
At the U.S. Gulf, one percent was stable at $15.25-50, while three percent rose slightly to about $13.50 on reports Mexico was still looking for more HS barrels.
USG July three percent paper firmed slightly with crude to near the $14 level, traders said.

New York city gate gas prices were steady to down slightly Tuesday to the low-$2.40s/mmBtu, or $15.31 a barrel equivalent. Gas at Henry Hub, the NYMEX delivery point, showed a similar move to the $2.16/mmBtu area, or $13.61 a barrel.
